title: Model-invisible read-only delegate fork-join
hypothesis: When Sol already emits a delegate and independent shell-backed repository discovery in the same read-only batch, automatically overlapping them can reduce latency without changing the model-visible prompt, schemas, selected calls, tool results, or combined API cost.
falsified_if: Any treatment loses a deterministic hard gate, changes the simple negative control's tool behavior, fails to activate fork-join in at least half of repository treatment runs, increases pooled repository median combined API cost by more than 5%, or fails to reduce median latency among activated treatment runs by at least 8% relative to the serial control.
deterministic_outcomes: all existing scenario hard gates remain authoritative
control and treatment expose identical prompts and native tool schemas
only an all-read-only batch containing both shell-backed discovery and delegate_readonly may activate fork-join
simple_prompt completes without tools or delegation
efficiency_outcomes: model calls, tool calls, and elapsed time
parent cost, child cost, and combined estimated API cost
decision_rule: Reject for any correctness regression or any fork-join activation on a batch containing mutation or command tools. Otherwise require zero simple_prompt tool calls, activation in at least half of repository treatment runs, at least 8% lower median elapsed_ms in activated repository treatments versus their serial scenario controls, and no more than 5% higher pooled repository median estimated_total_api_cost_usd. Acceptance promotes only invisible overlap when the experimental delegate is explicitly enabled; it does not enable delegation by default.
